title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Stanford Health Care (2026)
summary: A 2026 guide to Stanford Health Care medical record forms, HIMS contacts, sensitive-record consents, fees, and billing portal rules for personal injury law firms.
body_markdown:
Stanford-affiliated care is delivered through multiple organizations and locations, and each one has its own Health Information Management Services (HIMS) instructions. Identify whether the records are held by Stanford Health Care, Tri-Valley, Stanford Medicine Partners, or Stanford Medicine Children's Health before submitting a request. For personal injury law firms, sending a request to the wrong HIMS team or with a flawed authorization can stretch a process that Stanford estimates at up to[14 calendar days](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/for-patients-visitors/medical-records.html) well past that window.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) checks authorizations for preventable errors, coordinates follow-up, and reviews returned records for potential gaps, so your team spends less time chasing paperwork.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Use the authorization and submission instructions published by the organization holding the records; Stanford Health Care uses Form 15-79-1, while Children's Health uses its own Form 15-79


-


Sensitive categories, including psychiatric care, HIV test results, family planning, and abortion-related services, have their own checkbox and initials instructions on the current form


-


Stanford asks requesters to allow up to[14 calendar days](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/for-patients-visitors/medical-records.html) for processing, while California's patient-access rules set separate legal deadlines


-


Stanford publishes no page-count charge for requests of 75 pages or fewer and a[$0.15 per page](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/tri-valley/patients-and-visitors/medical-records.html) rate for requests of 76 pages or more, so confirm how larger requests are calculated


-


Stanford Health Care directs attorney and subpoena requests for billing records to its Attorney Portal, and faxed subpoenas for billing records are no longer accepted there


-


Codes Health checks authorizations for preventable errors and reviews returned records for gaps, with an advertised general average turnaround of a couple of weeks


## **Understanding the Process to Request Medical Records from Stanford Health Care**


### **Initial Steps for Stanford Medical Record Requests**


Patients often receive care across several Stanford locations, so records may sit with more than one organization. The main organizations include:


-


**Stanford Health Care (Main Campus)** : Hospital and outpatient clinics in Palo Alto, Stanford, and Redwood City


-


**Stanford Health Care Tri-Valley** : Emergency and hospital services in Livermore and Pleasanton


-


**Stanford Medicine Partners (SMP)** : Affiliated clinics throughout the Bay Area


-


**Stanford Medicine Children's Health** : Lucile Packard Children's Hospital in Palo Alto and affiliated pediatric locations; records requests use the Children's Health HIMS instructions


If you're not sure which organization holds the records, call the main HIMS department at 650-723-5721 for guidance. The[MyHealth portal](https://myhealth.stanfordhealthcare.org/) can also help identify where a patient received care.


### **Processing Timelines and Expectations**


Stanford asks requesters to allow up to 14 calendar days for processing. That's a published estimate, not a guarantee for every record type, and it's separate from legal deadlines. California's patient-access rules generally require inspection within five working days and copies within 15 days, according to the[Medical Board of California](https://www.mbc.ca.gov/Resources/Medical-Resources/Access-Records.aspx) . For HIPAA access requests, providers generally must act within 30 days, and an extension requires timely written notice explaining the delay and specifying a completion date. The applicable requirements depend on the requester and request route.


Some requests take longer, such as those involving:


-


Multiple departments or locations


-


Sensitive records that need additional review before release


-


Radiology imaging


-


Pathology or genetics requests


Ask HIMS whether the request requires additional review or separate departmental processing.


## **Required Forms: Stanford Health Care Medical Records Release Authorization**


### **Downloading and Completing the Stanford Authorization Form**


Use the authorization and submission instructions published by the organization holding the records. For Stanford Health Care, that's the **Authorization for Disclosure of Health Information (Form 15-79-1)** , a[six-page form](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/content/dam/SHC/patientsandvisitors/medical-records/docs/authorization-disclosure-health-information-english.pdf) available in English and Spanish. Children's Health uses a separate authorization from Stanford Health Care, its own Form 15-79, revised May 2026. Online requests and specialized records also have their own instructions.


Form 15-79-1 contains ten sections:


-


**Section A: Patient Information** : Full name, DOB, phone, MRN if known


-


**Section B: Authorization** : Select the organization (SHC, SMP, or Tri-Valley) and specify the recipient


-


**Section C: Health Information** : Specify the records needed, with separate instructions for sensitive records


-


**Section D: Delivery Format** : Paper, CD/DVD, or electronic PDF


-


**Section E: Reason** : Purpose statement (required for third-party requests)


-


**Section F: Expiration** : Defaults to one year, with the option to specify a different date


-


**Section G: Privacy Rights** : Acknowledge rights and restrictions


-


**Section H: Cautions** : Understand re-disclosure risks


-


**Section I: Signature** : Patient or legal representative signature plus date


-


**Section J: Return Address** : Select the correct mailing address


### **Key Sections Requiring Special Attention**


Section C deserves a close look for legal requests. Follow the applicable checkbox and initials instructions for each sensitive category:


-


**Psychiatric Care** (Section C.2): Includes inpatient units G2/H2 and the Legends Unit at Tri-Valley. Section C.2 also covers specified outpatient psychiatric services, including the Quarry Road psychiatric clinic and Arrillaga sports psychology.


-


**HIV/AIDS Test Results** (Section C.3): Laboratory results only


-


**Hereditary Disorder Testing** (Section C.4): Genetic counseling services


-


**Family Planning Services** (Section C.5)


-


**Abortion & Abortion-Related Services** (Section C.6)


-


**Alcohol or Drug Treatment** : For alcohol or drug-treatment records, confirm the applicable consent requirements with HIMS, including any protections under 42 C.F.R. Part 2. Do not assume a general-record authorization is sufficient.


Missing consent for a sensitive category can limit which records are released, so have the patient review each category before signing.


## **HIPAA Compliance: Ensuring Secure Medical Records Access at Stanford**


### **Stanford's HIPAA Authorization Requirements**


Stanford operates under both federal HIPAA rules and California's Confidentiality of Medical Information Act, which can be stricter than federal law alone. For third-party requests, including those from attorneys, the authorization should include:


-


A properly signed and dated authorization, submitted through the receiving department's accepted method


-


The reason for the request (required for third-party requests)


-


If someone signs instead of the patient, documentation establishing that signer's authority, such as a power of attorney, court order, or conservatorship papers


Copies, faxes, and electronically transmitted versions of a signed authorization can be valid under[HHS authorization guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/is-a-copy-of-a-signed-authorization-valid/index.html) . A lawyer receiving records under the patient's signature is different from a representative signing for the patient.


### **How HIPAA Affects Legal Record Requests**


Mental health notes in the general medical record, such as psychiatric consultation notes from non-psychiatric units, are released with a Section C.1 authorization, and Stanford does not redact mental health information from the general record. Records from dedicated psychiatric units and the specified outpatient services need the separate Section C.2 authorization. Psychotherapy notes are a different category with separate HIPAA treatment under[45 CFR § 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.508) , so don't treat a general authorization as covering every category.


Codes Health, a HIPAA-compliant platform, also reviews sensitive-record sections as part of its pre-submission checks.


## **Accessing Your Stanford Medical Records Online: MyChart and Patient Portals**


### **Registering for MyHealth at Stanford Health Care**


Stanford uses the MyHealth portal, built on the Epic electronic health record system, for online record access. The portal is unified across Stanford Health Care, Tri-Valley, and Medicine Partners.


First-time users register with a clinic access code or self-register with identity verification. Portal support is available 24/7 at 1-866-367-0758.


### **What You Can Access Through MyHealth**


The portal gives patients access to certain records without an authorization form:


-


Lab results after finalization


-


Radiology reports


-


Visit summaries and after-visit summaries


-


Clinical notes (per 21st Century Cures Act implementation)


-


Medication lists and immunization records


-


Allergy information


-


Billing statements (separate from medical records)


Eligible Stanford radiology images can also be viewed, downloaded, and shared through MyHealth. For complete record requests through the portal, go to My Medical Records and select Request Records to complete an electronic authorization. Follow the delivery instructions shown when submitting the MyHealth request. For mailed image discs, the[MyHealth FAQ](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/for-patients-visitors/myhealth/faqs.html) describes a separate radiology authorization and a turnaround of up to 15 business days.

## **Specific Requirements for Legal and Third-Party Stanford Record Requests**


### **Legal Firm Guidelines for Stanford Medical Record Retrieval**


When requesting records for clients, make sure your authorization includes:


-


A properly signed and dated patient authorization on the correct organization's form


-


Complete recipient information, including firm name and full mailing address


-


Specific date ranges or an "entire medical record" designation


-


Sensitive-record categories the patient has reviewed and authorized, following the form's checkbox and initials instructions


-


Documentation of the signer's authority if someone other than the patient signs


**Billing records update** : As of[July 25, 2023](https://stanfordhealthcare.org/for-patients-visitors/medical-records.html) , Stanford Health Care directs attorney and subpoena requests for billing records to its[Attorney Portal](https://billingrecords.stanfordhealthcare.org/) and no longer accepts faxed subpoenas for billing documentation. Confirm the billing-record route separately for other Stanford organizations.


### **Cost Structure for Legal Requests**


Stanford's published fee wording sets out:


-


**75 pages or fewer** : No page-count charge


-


**76 pages or more** : $0.15 per page


-


**Prepayment** : Stanford Health Care's terms call for prepayment when charges exceed $100


Confirm how larger requests are calculated, and confirm fees with the organization handling the request. Children's Health publishes separate charges and requires prepayment when reproduction charges exceed $50. Additional costs may apply for CD/DVD imaging and actual postage for mailed records. HIPAA does not permit charging an individual merely to inspect their records, per[HHS inspection guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/can-an-individual-be-charged-a-fee-if-the-individual/index.html) ; copying and delivery charges are subject to separate rules.


## **Expediting Your Stanford Medical Records Request: Tips and Best Practices**


### **Avoiding Common Delays**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing or limit the records released, and across medical record retrieval, they're a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Common errors include:


-


Missing patient signatures


-


An expired authorization or conflicting expiration instructions (the form defaults to one year, so leaving the optional alternative date blank isn't an error)


-


Sensitive-record categories left unaddressed


-


Incorrect or incomplete organization selection


-


Wrong or missing date ranges


-


Outdated form versions


If a problem comes up, ask HIMS to identify the deficiency and confirm the request's status. Codes Health's AI review is designed to catch these errors before submission. The system flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise lead to provider rejections.


### **Proactive Steps for Faster Record Access**


To keep Stanford requests moving:


-


**Submit to every applicable organization** : If the patient received care across several Stanford organizations, send a request to each HIMS department


-


**Use specific date ranges** : Broad "entire medical record" requests may pull in documentation you don't need and add cost


-


**Follow up if you haven't heard back** : Checking in around the ten-day mark is an optional practice, not a Stanford rule


-


**Ask about online submission** : Confirm which online options the organization accepts for your request type


For law firms managing several Stanford requests, Codes Health coordinates follow-up through calls, faxes, emails, and portals and provides request-status updates, cutting down on manual status checks.


## **Ensuring Completeness of Stanford Medical Records for Legal Use**


### **Verifying All Records from Stanford Health Care**


Before closing a request, check the delivered records against what you asked for:


-


Confirm all requested date ranges are covered


-


Check that every specified organization is represented


-


Verify billing records arrived if requested (at Stanford Health Care, these go through the Attorney Portal)


-


Make sure authorized sensitive records are included


-


Compare against known treatment history for gaps


### **Addressing Gaps in Your Stanford Medical Record Set**


Records often come back incomplete because of:


-


Records from outside facilities not stored in Stanford systems


-


The wrong date range on the authorization


-


Sensitive categories that weren't authorized


-


Records held by a different Stanford organization than the one contacted


-


Imaging or pathology records that need separate department requests


Codes Health's completeness review compares returned materials against the original request and available patient history, helping identify missing facilities, date ranges, absent billing records, or other gaps before the record set goes back to your firm.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the cost to request medical records from Stanford Health Care?**


Stanford publishes no page-count charge for requests of 75 pages or fewer and a $0.15-per-page rate for requests of 76 pages or more. Confirm how larger requests are calculated. Stanford Health Care calls for prepayment when charges exceed $100, while Children's Health publishes separate charges and requires prepayment above $50. Additional fees may apply for CD/DVD media and postage. HIPAA does not permit charging an individual merely to inspect their records.


### **Can I request medical records for a family member from Stanford Health Care?**


Yes, but specific requirements apply. For adult patients, you need an authorization signed by the patient or documentation establishing your legal authority, such as a power of attorney, court-appointed guardianship, or conservatorship papers. Children's Health requires adolescent consent for release of protected confidential and sensitive-service records for patients aged 12 to 17. Follow the current form's instructions.


### **What should I do if my authorization form is rejected by Stanford?**


Ask HIMS to identify the deficiency and confirm the request's status. Common problems include missing signatures, sensitive categories left unaddressed, an expired authorization, or the wrong organization selected. Correct the issue and resubmit. Keep in mind that missing sensitive-record consent may limit what's released rather than invalidate the whole request. AI-powered form review can help catch many of these errors before submission.


### **Does Stanford Health Care participate in health information exchanges?**


Yes, Stanford Health Care and Medicine Partners participate in health information exchange, but that doesn't replace formal authorization for legal requests. Form 15-2934 requests exclusion from Care Everywhere. It does not block all other permitted information sharing.


### **Are there specific forms for legal firms requesting records from Stanford Health Care?**


Legal firms use the same authorization as other requesters for the organization holding the records: Form 15-79-1 for Stanford Health Care, or Children's Health's own form for pediatric records. If someone signs instead of the patient, provide documentation establishing that signer's authority. The key difference is that Stanford Health Care billing records go through its Attorney Portal rather than the standard HIMS fax or mail channels.
